title: Choose the parcel journey layout
question: The product flow and Meesho-inspired visual cues are confirmed. Which screen structure should carry the prototype? Compare how clearly it shows one parcel, all four roles, and both outcome branches. The images are high-fidelity layout mockups, not build screenshots.

options.label: Guided journey stage
options.lineage: One parcel, presented as a live walkthrough
options.thesis: Move through the parcel story one decision at a time, with one role's working screen in focus.
options.viewport: A checkout-to-delivery rail anchors the top; the role view fills the center; the parcel event log and branch controls stay visible below.
options.case: The presenter can guide judges from checkout to either outcome without losing the parcel's current state.
options.risk: Switching roles is explicit; viewers may not see every role's screen at once.

options.label: Shared parcel workbench
options.lineage: Operations workspace with role-specific companion views
options.thesis: Keep parcel status, owner, next action and full history in a persistent operations workspace.
options.viewport: The selected parcel and journey stage lead; event history occupies the main column; operations action and linked rider/customer preview sit alongside.
options.case: Strongest for explaining system ownership and showing how a role action changes the same record.
options.risk: Can feel more like an admin dashboard than a complete customer experience.

options.label: Four-role handoff map
options.lineage: Service blueprint aligned by time and responsibility
options.thesis: Make every handoff visible by aligning Operations, Rider, Recipient and Nearby Buyer on one shared journey.
options.viewport: The parcel's stages run left to right and four labeled role lanes run top to bottom, with actions and outcomes aligned at each handoff.
options.case: Makes the shared system and branch logic obvious in a single glance.
options.risk: Dense on small screens; each role's interface is less immersive in the overview.
